why: The TSD P6 v2 outranks the legacy story for the module API and names no POST /admin/reference-loads path, so the story cannot cite the P4 endpoint as its provided operation, while the legacy checks and the refusal messages still have to be proved.

impact: Text only: two rows of section 14 change and no code, contract shape or test data changes.

text: rwb-comms reads the proof-of-delivery records of a business date with GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP07/records and the batch status, the feed version and the stale marker with GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness on the P1 rwb-source-data contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout; the row carries the barcode, the sent date, the notice reference, the callback date, the delivery status and the sent type, and no row of a date is read unless the freshness answer for that date is COMPLETE.
why: P6 has no grant on recovery.v_ace_pod or v_ace_batch_status after the split, and neither the Ownership Map nor the architecture extract names the P1 element that serves them; without one named read the consumed row, the fake and the four criteria that assert a delivery cannot be tested.
read: Ownership Map v1 (P1 rows, no v_ace_* grant to P6); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 notes; FSD P6 v3 change note; RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG section 12.2.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-source-data owner, in the baseline review of RWB-P6-E1055-CON.
impact: If P1 publishes another path, the product code or another field set, one consumed row, the pod client adapter and one fake change; no schema, event or workflow change.

text: The Litigation area and the R right declared on the notice read are enforced at gateway-bff on the screen path, and the operation itself is called with a service identity from the composite route; where a local guard is required, it is the platform guard library and not a guard written in rwb-comms, and a refusal keeps MSG-P4-002 and changes nothing.
why: DP-08 is not in the patterns of legacy RWB-E1-055 and no rwb-access story is a build or contract dependency of the key, while the TSD declares a capability area and a right on the operation; the enforcement point has to be stated for the access test case to have a subject.
read: TSD P6 v2 T6.1 and T-A.2 (API-P6-002); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-08; Ownership Map v1 P4 api rows; legacy RWB-E1-055 section 10.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access owner and the gateway-bff owner.
impact: If a local guard is required, one platform guard dependency and one refusal test path are added; no table, event or workflow change.

text: The stored letter of a notice is read with GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId} on the P5 rwb-document contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and a notice whose letter cannot be read is held rather than dispatched; the letter is the claim-check artefact the INT-14 record references and no file content enters a workflow input.
why: The INT-14 record set carries a document reference and the loop must know the letter exists, while no source names the document operation or its answer shape.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 notes; TSD P6 v2 T3.3 (notice.document_id to document); RWB-ITG-E1055-ITG section 12.2.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-document owner, in the baseline review of RWB-P6-E1055-CON.
impact: If the document hub returns a handle rather than metadata, the generate-letter activity and one fake change; no schema or event change.

text: The INT-14 and INT-15 fixed layouts, their record keys, the file naming and the SFTP transport are the WIN owner's specifications and are attached to the contract baseline as a versioned annex; until the annex is attached the file element of the baseline declares the fields, the business date, the feed version, the trailer and the batch-status gate as a shape only, and every synthetic fixture file is derived from the annex.
why: The loop cannot be built against WIN without a layout, and inventing one would fix a value no source gives; the annex keeps the layout with its owner and the baseline keeps the shape.
read: TSD P6 v2 T5.1 (INT-14); legacy RWB-E1-055 sections 4, 12 and 16; FSD P6 v3 A2.2.
confirm: Solution architect with the WIN owner and the rwb-integration owner before the SIT cutover.
impact: A layout change is a new file version and a fixture update; it changes no table, event or workflow element.

text: rwb-comms computes the barcode break on its own notice rows three days after the sent date and exposes it as a break, and rwb-source-data owns the References exception list and the data-quality read that shows both on SCR-45; the platform administrator reads the break, and no service writes another service's exception row.
why: The barcode and the sent date are P6's and the data-quality read is P1's, and no source rules which one runs REC-05; a stated split lets both stories build without a shared table.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-055 sections 4, 5 and 8; Ownership Map v1 (reconciliation_result P1, notice P6).
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data owner and the data steward.
impact: If P1 runs REC-05, the break moves to the P1 story and the P6 reconciliation becomes a read; one operation and one test move, with no schema change.

text: The WIN SFTP host, port, network zone, certificate subject and owner, the staging and file-store container names, the retention period, the file size and object counts of a batch, the worker pool sizes and the scaler caps are reviewed values per environment, recorded in the provisioning artefacts and confirmed with the WIN owner, Security and the platform team before the SIT cutover.
why: No source gives any of them, and the provisioning cannot ship without a value; every value stays an environment entry and none is compiled or committed as a constant.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 44; legacy RWB-E1-055 sections 3 and 17; Template and Rules v1 §R9.
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure with Security and the WIN owner.
impact: A change of host, zone, size or cap is an environment change and a runbook line; no code, contract or schema change.

text: rwb-comms is deployed into the Recovery namespace of the platform with one dispatch Schedule at 16:00 Asia/Bangkok, overlap SKIP and the catch-up window of the workflow kit, and the JOB-10 handoff is the bank Airflow file window opening the WIN edge for the business date and passing that date to the Schedule; no Quartz row, shared job table entry or Control-M job exists.
why: DL35 is open and no source names the slot, the namespace, the Schedule name or the Airflow task, while the deployment check and the runbook need one stated mechanism to assert.
read: TSD P6 v2 appendix T-B (DL35); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 notes; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10.
confirm: DevOps lead with the platform team under DL35 and the Airflow owner.
impact: A different slot or a different handoff changes the values files, the registration step and one runbook entry; no code change.

text: The alert values are provisional until UAT: the file of the business date alerts when it is not delivered two hours after the 16:00 window or when the handshake fails twice, the pod batch alerts when the freshness answer is not COMPLETE by 09:00 on the business day after it was due, the dispatch count alerts when no file is built inside the window while notices are eligible, and the outbox lag alerts above five minutes.
why: No source gives a threshold, an interval or a reviewed time, and the deployment cannot ship without one; every value stays a values-file entry with a runbook line.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; legacy RWB-E1-055 sections 8 and 16; FSD P6 v3 A2.2 VR-P6-002-1.
confirm: DevOps lead with the rwb-comms service owner and the platform observability owner at UAT.
impact: A threshold change is a values-file change and one runbook line; no code, contract or schema change.

text: hold_reason is a versioned reference list whose only named value is TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN; any other hold writes the free-text reason of the holding rule until the business owner publishes the list, and the Held state keeps the notice out of the file without changing the case.
why: The field exists and the Held state is part of the model, but the sources name one value only, and a fabricated list would fix a business value no source gives.
read: FSD P6 v3 A2.2 AC-EXC-P6-002-02; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-032, no LOV).
confirm: Business analyst P6 with the business owner before the Epic 2 refinements.
impact: Publishing the list adds one reference row set and one assertion; no schema, event or workflow change.
